summary: Unresponsive runtime sockets and elevated 5xx during tenant priority surge
description:
Issue summary:
During a high-priority tenant ramp at ~2026-03-10T14:30 UTC customer observed elevated 5xx responses (502/503) and a subset of streaming sessions dropping with runtime processes reporting 'socket read timeout' and reduced accept queue depth. Impact: customer tenant experienced degraded throughput and increased latency across chat and embedding endpoints.

Impact:
- PapertrailAI reported ~18% of requests returned 502/503 over a 12-minute window.
- Long-lived streaming sessions dropped; reconnect attempts saw retry amplification.
- No billing discrepancy observed; throughput throttles triggered for the tenant.

Environment:
- Prod cluster in us-east: mix of dedicated and shared GPU nodes serving the tenant via a weighted route.
- Route config: tenant pinned to route-weight group beta-weighted-3 with fallback to general-pool.

Steps to reproduce (customer-reported):
1) Start high-concurrency test against /v1/chat/stream with 80 concurrent streams pinned to the tenant.
2) Simultaneously submit embedding bulk uploads to /v1/embeddings with small batches (~16 per request).
3) After ~8-10 minutes observe increased connection resets and 502/503 responses.

Observed logs (excerpt):
- runtime[worker-21] WARN socket read timeout (fd=1024) after 30000ms
- proxy[acceptor] DEBUG accept-queue-depth dropped from 1024 -> 128 in 90s
- runtime[monitor] ERROR ephemeral runtime heartbeat missed, initiating drain
- api-gateway WARN upstream returned 502: connection reset by peer

Notes: This pattern differs from usual GPU OOM or kernel fallback; traces point to an accept-queue drain along with a runtime-side slowdown (socket stalls) that amplified apigw backpressure and hedged retries.
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: a surge in tenant-priority traffic triggered a priority rebalancer event that concurrently initiated transient connection draining on a subset of ephemeral proxies. That drain reduced accept queue depth on front-line proxies and forced excess hedged retries into a small number of runtimes causing socket stalls and TLS handshake backlog.

What we checked: 
- Health checks: ephemeral worker heartbeats for affected node pool show repeated 1–2s delays starting at 2026-03-10T14:25 UTC.
- Kernel metrics: no immediate kernel fallback events or NVML resets; GPU memory not saturated.
- Network: intermediate proxies reported increases in SYN_RECV and reduced free file descriptors on the worker process.
- Routing: weighted-route shift occurred at 2026-03-10T14:20 UTC (auto-rebalance policy).

Partial findings: 
- Accept queue collapse correlated with a concurrent config sweep that toggled priority windows for the tenant.
- Runtimes entered a slow syscall path (observed via strace sampling) when faced with >200 concurrent ephemeral TLS handshakes while the accept queue was depleted.

Logs & dashboards referenced: 
- Grafana: /dashboards/d/accept-queue/accept-queue-us-east (spike at 14:25)
- Loki: cluster/us-east/runtime/error stream (query ref: #L-309481-14)
- Slack: #support thread T05B3K2 (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05B3K2/p167?)
comments: Priya Rao (Support) — 2026-03-10T15:05Z: Acknowledged with PapertrailAI; requested request IDs and timestamps for failed calls. Asked for temporary throttling to reduce concurrent streaming sessions.

Marco Chen (SRE) — 2026-03-10T15:32Z: Observed accept-queue depth collapse on proxy-ephemeral-12. Kicked off live capture and increased proxy keepalive timeout. Correlates with weighted-route rebalancer activity.
Action: Disabled route sweep for affected tenant to stabilize.

Lina Ortega (Runtime Eng) — 2026-03-10T16:10Z: Found high syscall latency in accept() path when fd table approached 90% usage on runtime-worker processes. Proposed two mitigations: (1) increase ephemeral proxy accept queue and fd soft limits; (2) add backpressure at api-gateway for hedged retries.
workarounds:
- Disabled weighted-route sweep for PapertrailAI to prevent further rebalances.
- Applied temporary proxy accept-queue increase on us-east front-line proxies.
- Advised customer to reduce concurrent streaming sessions to <40 until fix is deployed.
- Enabled hedged-retry rate limiter on the route to prevent amplified fanout.
resolution:
In progress — short-term mitigations applied stabilized error rate to <1% within 12 minutes. Medium-term fix planned: adjust rebalancer cooldown to avoid simultaneous drain on multiple proxies and harden runtime accept() path to pre-allocate file descriptors for TLS handshakes.

Follow-ups scheduled: 
- SRE to deploy rebalancer cooldown patch to staging on 2026-03-13 (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/5021).
- Runtime team to land fd-prealloc change in canary: planned 2026-03-15.
- Postmortem to be authored in Confluence and shared with PapertrailAI by 2026-03-18.
resolution_status: Stabilized with mitigations; root-cause analysis ongoing
notes: Customer impact prioritized due to dedicated tier SLA. No data exfiltration suspected. Billing unaffected. Recommend adding an automated pre-check in route weighter to ensure accept-queue headroom before rebalancer operations.
